extracted.intended_audience: health reporters, editors, and newsrooms (members or users of AHCJ guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and producing health reporting: which topics to cover, ethical constraints, and the factors and quality markers that make a health story newsworthy and reliable according to the Association of Health Care Journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject hospital arrangements that improperly influence coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject hospital arrangements that improperly influence coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/ethics position emphasizing independence from payer/provider influence; avoid agreements that compromise impartial reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist confidentiality agreements with hospitals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept gag or confidentiality clauses that limit full reporting or transparency about health care institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose secrecy clauses in medical-device-manufacturer contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose secrecy clauses in medical-device-manufacturer contracts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid arrangements that prevent disclosure of safety, performance, or contractual terms related to medical devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification of health claims required
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent verification of health claims required
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify health claims through independent sources rather than relying solely on company or single-study press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Areas (Topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics considered within AHCJ's scope: Drug approvals / FDA actions; Clinical trials; Public health alerts (outbreaks, recalls); Hospital ratings and quality; Insurance / costs; Mental health; Disparities (race, gender, geography); Aging and end-of-life; Pandemics (COVID, etc.); Reproductive health; Substance use; Pharma industry; Medical devices; Telemedicine; Health policy / Medicare / Medicaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topic areas represent beats and subject-matter areas AHCJ prioritizes as newsworthy for health reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health threat — magnitude of risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Public health threat — magnitude of risk
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how large and immediate the health threat is to determine newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number affected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the scope and scale of people impacted when judging the story's importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of outcome (mortality, morbidity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the seriousness of potential outcomes — death, long-term harm, disability — as a newsworthiness factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerable populations disproportionately affected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to stories that show unequal impacts on children, elderly, low-income groups, racial/ethnic minorities, or other vulnerable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy implications — coverage decisions, regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories with implications for health policy, coverage, reimbursement, or regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability — provider/insurer/pharma misconduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness increases when reporting can expose wrongdoing, conflicts, or system failures deserving scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research quality — peer-reviewed, sample size, replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Research quality — peer-reviewed, sample size, replication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge studies by methodological rigor and reproducibility; single weak studies should not be overhyped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost story — affordability angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider economic impact and patient affordability as central elements of the story's relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparities exposed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight inequities in access, outcomes, or treatment across populations as a newsworthy dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient story — humanizing data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use individual patient experiences to illustrate broader data and make stories relatable, while safeguarding privacy and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: New treatment — efficacy, side effects, access
rubrics_metrics.description: New treatment — efficacy, side effects, access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on new therapies with balanced coverage of benefits, harms, and access barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency — outbreak, recall
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize urgent events — disease outbreaks, product recalls — that require rapid public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple independent expert sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more than one qualified, independent expert to corroborate claims and provide context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient voices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives of patients and caregivers to contextualize the human impact of health issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical literacy — relative vs. absolute risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical literacy — relative vs. absolute risk
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain statistics clearly; distinguish relative from absolute risks and provide appropriate denominators and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state study limitations, uncertainties, and what is not yet known to avoid overstating findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest of sources noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest of sources noted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding, ties, or incentives that could bias studies or expert commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language explanation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate technical findings into accessible language for general audiences without losing accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hype — single-study breakthroughs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about promoting 'breakthrough' claims from isolated studies; provide balanced context and skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update health stories as evidence evolves
rubrics_metrics.description: Update health stories as evidence evolves
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat health reporting as iterative; correct and update coverage when new, credible evidence emerges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threat scale and immediacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how large the threat is and how quickly it impacts populations as a core criterion for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable evidence base
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor stories grounded in verifiable, reproducible evidence rather than hearsay or unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient/community impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tangible effects on patients and communities, including care access and everyday consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: System accountability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether reporting holds health systems, institutions, or companies responsible for failures or harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity dimension
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and highlight disparities and equity implications in healthcare delivery and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical actionability for readers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information readers can use — prevention steps, when to seek care, how to navigate systems — without offering medical advice beyond expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-misinformation value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories that correct falsehoods or reduce harmful misinformation in health topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to reporting that could prompt policy, regulatory, or system reforms improving public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHCJ awards recognition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: AHCJ Awards Categories: recognize excellence in health investigative reporting, beat reporting, consumer/feature, public health, business, and online journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the types of reporting AHCJ values and rewards; useful as exemplar categories for high-quality work.
